policies: Ordinary main pools contain train items only. The sidecar is authoritative for frame and split metadata; heldout items must not be copied into train memberships.
Uniformly sample the same frame inventory for both categories. Balance tones, A/B assignment and voice profiles independently; a favorite-word weighting may reintroduce a shortcut.

Cross-word ABX always requires X to be a different lexical word from A and B. Prefer A/B on the same segmental frame and X on another, or three distinct frames; do not correlate the answer with a shared reference/X frame.

Use reserved words as X against familiar training-frame references, counterbalanced across tones, for a lexical-frame transfer check. Alternatively use one heldout frame for both references and the other for X, but this exposes reserved words. Record exposure and never reuse a demonstrated item as previously unheard.

No hints or feedback during the first transfer check. Two heldout frames are a limited diagnostic sample, not a validated mastery measure; ordinary listening outside the app and historical exposure are unknown.

IPA is broad editorial transcription. /ʂɻ̩/ represents the shi syllable; /jɛn/ the yan syllable; /iŋ/ is a broad ying rhyme without committing to all surface glide/vowel variants. The same declared segmental form is used for each tone on a frame.

Tone3 uses the pedagogical /˨˩˦/ citation symbol; natural isolated T3 may have variable rise and creak. Do not force a fully rising tail in every connected-speech context or certify recordings by pitch tracing alone.
Do not concatenate these clips to construct sandhi or disyllabic lessons. Contextual tone material requires a separately authored and reviewed corpus.
Primary dictionary facts support selected readings and senses, not Putonghua audio approval, word-frequency rankings, or a license to redistribute dictionary recordings.

Retained spelling/IPA/meaning/romanization identities are preserved where possible. Changed comparison memberships and source context require fresh review; never transfer an old pass automatically to a different audio hash.
